results.title: Access Tokens for Meta Technologies
results.snippet:
An access token is an opaque string that identifies a user, app, or Facebook Page and can be used by the app to make Graph API calls. The token includes information about when it expires and which app generated it. Most API calls on Meta apps require an access token for privacy checks. Different types of access tokens support different use cases.

| Access Token Type | Description |
|---|---|
| App Access Token | App access tokens let you read and modify app settings. Generate one using your Meta app secret via a server-to-server call. |
| Client Token | Client tokens identify your app when calling app-level APIs from native or desktop apps. Because client tokens are embedded in apps, they are not secret. Find your client token in the Meta App Dashboard. |
| Page Access Token | Page access tokens let you read, write, and modify data belonging to a Facebook Page. To obtain one, first get a user access token, then exchange it for a Page access token via the Graph API. |
| System User Access Token | System User access tokens let your app perform programmatic, automated actions on Ad objects or Pages without requiring input from an app user or re-authentication. |

Today, we're announcing updates to **Ads Management Standard Access (AMSA)** — the App Review feature that unlocks higher Marketing API rate limits, system user quotas, and other enhanced capabilities for your app.
Based on developer feedback, we're making three key improvements: (1) renaming the feature for clarity; (2) revising the qualification threshold; and (3) making eligibility criteria fully transparent in the product UI.
**These changes take effect on May 4, 2026.** This is not a breaking change — no code updates are required, and existing access levels are preserved automatically.
## “Ads Management Standard Access” is now "Marketing API Access Tier"
The AMSA feature is being renamed to “**Marketing API Access Tier”** feature.
The old name caused persistent confusion: developers frequently mixed AMSA up with the separate `ads_management` permission. The new name clearly communicates what this feature controls — your app's tier of access to Marketing API functionality.

| **Before** | **After** |
|---|---|
| Feature: "Ads Management Standard Access" | Feature: **"Marketing API Access Tier"** |
| Lower tier: "Standard Access" | Lower tier: **"Limited Access"** |

results.title: Basic Ad Creation
results.snippet:
The Marketing API provides several endpoints to create and manage advertising campaigns. The primary creation endpoints include `campaigns`, `adsets`, and `ads`. This document describes these endpoints and what they do.
The `campaigns`, `adsets`, `ads`, and `adcreatives` endpoints support idempotent requests, so you can retry a failed create request without creating a duplicate object. See [Idempotent requests](/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/idempotent-requests).
### The `campaigns` endpoint
Use the [`campaigns` endpoint](/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/reference/ad-account/campaigns) to create and manage campaigns. Use this endpoint to set the overall objectives for your marketing efforts, such as brand awareness or conversions.
**Example API request:**
```
curl -X POST \
https://graph.facebook.com/v27.0/act_<AD_ACCOUNT_ID>/campaigns \
-F 'name=My Campaign' \
-F 'objective=LINK_CLICKS' \
-F 'status=PAUSED' \
-F 'access_token=<ACCESS_TOKEN>'
```

This guide assumes you have:
- An [ad account with Meta⁠](https://adsmanager.facebook.com/adsmanager/) with a valid payment method

To make successful calls to all endpoints in this guide, you will need:

- `ads_management`
- `pages_manage_ads`
- `pages_read_engagement`
- `pages_show_list`

- `OUTCOME_LEADS`
- `OUTCOME_SALES`
- `OUTCOME_TRAFFIC`
- `special_ad_categories`

results.title: Connect AI agents to Meta with MCP
results.snippet:
Meta runs official remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that bring Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Meta Ads capabilities to your agentic workflows.
**This page is documentation, not an MCP server.** Don’t add this page’s URL to your MCP client. Use one of these server URLs instead:
- Meta Ads MCP: `https://mcp.facebook.com/ads`
- Meta Social Technologies MCP: `https://mcp.facebook.com/devtools`
- WhatsApp Business Tools MCP: `https://mcp.facebook.com/whatsapp_business_tools`
## Benefits
- **One protocol, built for agent workflows.** Your agent connects to a Meta MCP server and discovers available tools at runtime. Tool descriptions, parameter schemas, and error responses are designed for large language models (LLMs) to interpret correctly. This design minimizes hallucination and failed tool calls.
- **Standard authentication.** OAuth-based authentication with permissions that you control from your Meta account settings. Each server defines its own permissions, so check the server-specific page for the ones it requests. Revoke access at any time.

Use this guide to connect a supported AI client to a remote Meta MCP server and authorize access with OAuth. When you finish, your client can discover and execute the server’s available tools.
## Before you begin
To connect a client, you need:
- A current version of a supported AI client.
- A Meta account with access to the assets that the server manages. Assets are the businesses, apps, and accounts that you select when you grant consent.
- A Meta app, only if the server-specific page requires a client ID.
Open the documentation for the MCP server that you want to use, starting from the [list of available Meta MCP servers](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/mcp#available-mcp-servers). A client is supported on a given server only if that server’s page lists it.

Use a developer-provided client ID when the server-specific page requires one, or when the server doesn’t recognize your client. Follow that page’s instructions to create or configure a Meta app, including its redirect URI. Then use the app’s **App ID** as the OAuth client ID.
